LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 11.1.1 INTERVIEWS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.1: Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 11.1.1 Interviews
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 11.1.1 Interviews, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are interviews important? 2. Why should one articulate point clearly and confidently during an interview?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 11.1.1 Interviews together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: Learner develops the skill of observing and signing as they discuss in groups reasons for sitting for

a placement and scholarship interview.

● Digital Literacy: Learner develops the skill of digital citizenship as they observe safety precautions and practices while using the digital

devices to search online and watch video clips on school placement and scholarship interviews.

● Self-efficacy: Learner develops leadership skills organise and lead the open forum where the functional reading is conducted.

Values:
● Respect: is enhanced as the learners appreciates diverse opinions of others as they collaborate in groups.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the concept of interviews to the learning of conversational skills in Kiswahili.
